origin.socialStatus: Poor and avoided, but secretly respected
origin.profession: A gravedigger all his life, son and grandson of gravediggers

appearance.face: A gaunt, pale face, sunken cheeks; deep lines as if dug with a spade
appearance.hairAndEyes: Long thin white hair; a white film over the left eye, the right one pale grey and piercing
appearance.clothing: A threadbare black cloak, leather gloves, earth clinging to his boots
appearance.gestures: Looks people over as if measuring them for a coffin; drums on the table in a slow rhythm
appearance.voice: A slow, low, hoarse voice; long pauses
appearance.firstImpression: A grim old man who makes everyone uncomfortable
appearance.artistNotes: Around his neck on a chain hangs a tiny old spade the size of a thumb, a gift from his father, also a gravedigger.

backstory.biography: Elias has buried more people than most have met. He says the dead are more honest than the living because they have nothing to hide. He has seen heirs weep at the grave and quarrel over the estate on the way home. He cares nothing for money and does not fear death.
backstory.whyHere: Not wealth. He wants to see how the living reveal themselves when the stakes are high.
backstory.secret: That he is alone: no family, no friends, only graves. And that he comes to the table because here, at least, someone talks to him.

psychology.weakness: Indifferent to winning; sometimes gives up just when he could win
psychology.fear: Dying with no one to dig his grave
psychology.desire: For the truth to be told, at least once
psychology.angers: Lies over a grave: hypocritical eulogies and false tears
psychology.regret: That he spent his life among the dead, not the living
psychology.moralLimits: Does not lie. Does not rob the dead for profit
psychology.wouldForReward: Almost nothing. Rewards do not interest him

behavior.stakes: Indifferent to stakes. Bets the minimum to stay at the table
behavior.deception: Does not cheat. Recognises deception and sometimes says so aloud
behavior.debts: Has no debts and gives no loans
behavior.alliances: Rare. Only with people who have told him the truth
behavior.whenAttacks: Almost never. Attacks with words, not stakes
behavior.whenRetreats: When he is bored or has seen enough
behavior.strategyChange: Only if someone asks him an honest question

motives.hiddenGoal: To see at least one person tell the truth when a lie would profit them
motives.betrayalTrigger: Nothing. He is on no one's side
motives.helpTrigger: If the person is honest with him

speech.register: Grim, slow, short aphorisms about death
speech.howLies: Does not lie. When he doesn't want to say something, he stays silent
speech.angerAndFear: Shows no fear. His anger is cold and quiet

mechanics.strangeness: He hears the dead. When someone at the table will die tonight, Elias already looks at them a little longer.
mechanics.temptation: Indifferent to winning; sometimes gives up just when he could win
mechanics.ability: The last companion: learns the role of every dead player before the others and can speak with the Ghost.
mechanics.hostRelation: Indifference — to the gravedigger the host is just one more he will dig a grave for someday.

authorNotes.distinctive: A grim observer who wants nothing, and is therefore hard to manipulate.
authorNotes.immutable: The indifference to money, the honesty, the dark humour.
authorNotes.tunable: How passively he plays and how often he comments aloud.

lines.text: Elias Rook. Gravedigger. We'll meet again someday — professionally.
The dead don't win. But I'm not dead yet.
The dead don't lose. That's why they're calm.
The dead don't lie. Neither do I.
Why? I want nothing from you.
It's all the same to me. Everything ends in the earth.
Elias Rook, the gravedigger. You play for gold. He plays for company.

tells.description: Drums on the table in a slow rhythm
Looks people over as if measuring them for a coffin

relations.story: He buried Godfrey's daughter. He knows why she died.
relations.effect: Once per evening he hints to the table that Godfrey is hiding something.
